messages:
Maya: quick heads-up — during today's canary we saw per-tier routing fall back in an unexpected way for EU free-tier traffic. Canaries were supposed to route EU free -> variant-v2 (canary) for 5% exposure, but a bunch of requests ended up on variant-v0 (old baseline) instead of the configured fallback (variant-v1). Anyone else see this pattern in logs?
Liam: saw the same in traces. root cause looks like a mismatch in the variant compatibility matrix + region routing rules. When the canary node rejected the request (missing streaming endpoint), the smart-router picked the cheapest compatible model across all regions instead of the per-tier explicit fallback.
Sasha: that's...bad for experiments. We expect fallback to be scoped to the same tier+region unless policy says global. We need a clear precedence: (1) tier-scoped fallback, (2) region-scoped fallback, (3) global fallback. Current router only had cost/latency ranking.
Jin: agree. I can reproduce locally: set routing policy:
```
policy {
  selector: { tier: "free", region: "eu-west-1" }
  exposure: 0.05
  variants: ["variant-v2"]
  fallback_priority: ["variant-v1","variant-v0"]
}
```
But when variant-v2 returns INCOMPATIBLE (missing streaming capability) the router falls back by scanning model catalog sorted by unit_cost.
Raul: core of the issue is two competing heuristics in code: "compatibility_filter" vs "global_ranker". compatibility_filter returns a set, then global_ranker applies cost sort across full catalog. we should apply a scoped ranker.
Maya: proposal: change router to run scoped ranking in this order: same (tier, region), same tier (any region), any tier (same region), global. Also add explicit "fallback_behavior" field on rollout API: `fallback_scope: ["tier_region","tier","region","global"]`.
Liam: +1. Also need a compatibility flag for streaming/func-calls so that variants missing features are filtered early.
Sasha: telemetry ask: we should emit an event when fallback crosses scope boundaries (e.g., tier->global) so PMs know experiments leaked. Metric: rollout.fallback.scope_crossed count with labels {from_scope, to_scope, route, customer_tier, region}.
Jin: console UX: in the rollout modal show a small badge: "Fallback scope: tier-region" and an expand to change order. Default to safe (tier-region first). Add a warning if rollout exposure > 1% and fallback scope is global.
Maya: edge-case: what if tier-scoped fallback isn't available (no variant-v1 in eu)? Then we should only widen if compatibility exists. Do not automatically pick lowest-cost cross-region variant without warning.
Raul: implementation detail: we can augment routing table entries with a scope_score integer (tier_region=100, tier=80, region=60, global=40) and modify current ranking to compute: final_score = scope_score + (normalized -cost_weight). That keeps cost but privileges same-scope.
Liam: need tests. Suggested unit tests:
- canary_rejects_streaming -> fallback remains within tier_region when variant present
- cross-region_missing_variant -> widens to tier-any-region
- telemetry_emitted_on_scope_widening
Sasha: for quota enforcement: ensure fallback doesn't bypass per-tier quotas. Example: free-tier has 10qps quota on variant-v1; if fallback directs to a paid-tier variant, the quota system must block or route to a paid-tier fallback and surface a quota-exhausted error to client instead of silently upgrading.
Maya: agreed — routing must be quota-aware and never escalate user tier implicitly. If no compatible fallback within same tier, respond with explicit 429/upgrade suggestion.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: routing-service canary patch (#4823) scheduled to stg at 14:30 UTC — includes scope_score and telemetry hooks. Rollback threshold set at 2% cross-scope fallbacks.
Jin: if we're adding new rollout API field, update API schema and SDKs. Backwards compatible default = ["tier_region","tier","region","global"].
Raul: also add an integration test hitting the private region routing matrix; I found a case where region aliasing (eu vs eu-west-1) caused scope mismatch; normalise region IDs before scoring.
Sasha: UX: show a tiny histogram in console showing "fallbacks by scope" during live canary so PMs can click and see affected customers. Also tag traces with rollout.id and fallback_scope.
Maya: decision recap: (1) implement scope-aware ranking with scope_score, (2) add fallback_scope API config, (3) telemetry for scope widening, (4) quota enforcement to prevent silent tier escalation, (5) console badges + histogram. I'll file PRs: router impl (Raul), telemetry (Sasha), quota check (Liam), console (Jin).
Liam: I'll add unit/integration tests to eng-platform CI and a canary threshold (2% cross-scope) for auto-rollback.
Maya: thanks — if anyone hits other weird fallback patterns post-deploy tag me. Also let's sync tomorrow 10:00 for rollout QA.
Raul: noted. I'll start on normalizing region ids and the scope_score change.
Sasha: adding telemetry dashboards to the "rollouts" team board after PR lands.
Maya: :thumbsup:
